summary.text: Benjamin Gilbert, listed by his party as Benjamin Gilbert, is the Greens candidate for Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election. He ran for the Greens in the federal seat of Indi in 2022, where he received about 3.6 per cent of first preferences. He describes himself as the father of two young children and puts climate action and renewable energy at the centre of his campaign.

priorities.text: I'm ready to campaign for immediate climate action, affordable and accessible housing
Urgent investment in renewable energy and sustainable infrastructure for rural communities
Dental and mental health care covered by Medicare

sources.title: Ovens Valley: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Benjamin Gilbert, Candidate for Ovens Valley, Australian Greens Victoria
Results of the 2022 Australian federal election in Victoria, Wikipedia

summary.text: Bronwyn (Bron) Murphy is standing for the Victorian Socialists in Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election. She works in hospitality, went to public schools in the region and has studied at La Trobe University. Her campaign focuses on cost of living and on better-resourced local schools, health and aged care.

priorities.text: More funding for public schools, more teachers on fair pay and smaller classes
Fully funded health and aged care available locally, without long trips
Secure housing and affordable groceries and energy for everyone

sources.title: Ovens Valley: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Bronwyn Murphy, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Carol Norton-Smith is the Family First candidate for Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. Her party profile says she comes from Sydney, settled in rural Victoria several years ago and teaches migrant medical professionals online, and that she takes part in the Catholic community where she lives. A candidate of the same name was second on Family First's Northern Victoria upper-house ticket at the 2022 state election.

occupation.text: Online teacher of migrant medical professionals

previous_candidacies.note: Same name and party, in the region that includes Ovens Valley; no source says this was the 2026 candidate. Second on the ticket.

priorities.text: Protecting unborn life, against both major parties' offer of free abortions
Opposing euthanasia to protect vulnerable older people
Cutting waste of public money and bureaucracy

sources.title: Carol Norton-Smith, Candidate for Ovens Valley, Family First Party

summary.text: James Rouel is One Nation's candidate for Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC reports that he holds a business degree and runs a rural food relief program reaching more than 5,000 people a month in over 20 towns on both sides of the Murray, in Victoria's north and the south of New South Wales. He was earlier an executive officer and event manager with the Bendigo Tennis Association. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

occupation.text: Leads a rural food relief program

sources.title: Ovens Valley: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Julian Fidge, a rural GP whose party says he opened a general practice in 2009 and a second, in South Wangaratta, in 2016, is the Libertarian candidate for Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election. His party says he was a pharmacist before training in medicine, served as an Army medical officer in East Timor, worked in the Rwandan refugee emergency and has been a CFA volunteer firefighter for over ten years; he also farms cattle. He has stood in Ovens Valley at each election since the seat was created, for the Country Alliance in 2014, the Country Party in 2018 and the Liberal Democrats in 2022, and ran in the federal seat of Indi in 2022. The party page also mentions an earlier council campaign.

occupation.text: General practitioner (rural GP) and cattle farmer

prior_roles.role: Medical officer, deployed to East Timor
Humanitarian work during the Rwandan refugee emergency

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's 2016 results list a Julian Fidge for the Australian Country Party in Indi, the party he stood for in Ovens Valley in 2018; no source we read confirms it is the same person.

priorities.text: Opposing tax increases and limits on personal liberty
A stronger say for regional communities in their own future
Access to health care and accountable government
Housing growth matched by local infrastructure
Interests listed by his party: AI safety, how councils work, nuclear energy and the use of judicial power

summary.text: Steve Manning is running as an independent in Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election, with the backing of the community group Voices for Ovens Valley. According to the ABC he works as an electrician and teaches at TAFE, and settled in the district roughly five years ago. He coaches senior football and netball teams at North Wangaratta and takes part in a local mental health project. We found no other published biography as at November 2026.

prior_roles.organisation: North Wangaratta Football and Netball Club

prior_roles.role: Participant in a local mental health initiative

sources.title: Ovens Valley: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Sue Litchfield is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Ovens Valley at the 2026 Victorian election. She is a support worker and longtime animal advocate who, her party says, volunteered with Choose Cruelty Free for 20 years and takes part in campaigns against horse racing and duck shooting. She stood for the party in Clarinda at the 2022 state election.

priorities.text: Stop animals being exploited in entertainment, sport and farming for food
Give animal welfare far more weight in government decisions
Protect wildlife and the environment, including from discarded fishing line and litter
Social justice, equality and inclusion, including for LGBTQIA+ people

sources.title: Sue Litchfield for Ovens Valley, Animal Justice Party Victoria

summary.text: Tim McCurdy is a Nationals MP who won Murray Valley in 2010 and has represented Ovens Valley since 2014. He left the shadow ministry in 2018 after being charged with fraud, charges a County Court judge dismissed in 2021, and returned to the frontbench after the 2022 election. He is now shadow minister for liquor and gaming, racing and veterans' affairs, and is recontesting Ovens Valley in 2026.

occupation.text: Dairy farmer and real estate agent

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Liquor and Gaming
prior_roles.note: Titled Gaming and Liquor from January 2025 to June 2026.

prior_roles.role: Nationals Whip in the Legislative Assembly
Shadow Assistant Minister for Regional Health and for Ambulance Services

prior_roles.note: Also held from June 2013 to March 2014.

prior_roles.role: Shadow Minister for Veterans and for Sport
Shadow Minister for Gaming and Liquor Regulation
Shadow parliamentary secretary, country schools and recreation
Parliamentary Secretary for Tourism and Trade

legal_and_integrity.text: A farm services company sued him for damages in the County Court, alleging misleading and unconscionable conduct.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: He settled the claim later in 2014.

legal_and_integrity.text: A former Nationals staffer brought harassment and bullying proceedings against him in the Magistrates' Court.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Settled confidentially; the settlement was paid by the Department of Parliamentary Services.

legal_and_integrity.text: Charged by Victoria Police with fraud offences dating from his time as a real estate agent; he stood down from the shadow ministry.
legal_and_integrity.outcome: Dismissed by the County Court in April 2021 for insufficient evidence, after the prosecution's main witness admitted falsifying the document.

priorities.text: A voice in Parliament for regional Victorians and farmers
Fair funding for regional areas
Better roads and transport in country areas
Helping more locals buy a home
The same education, sport and job opportunities for regional people as for those in the city

sources.title: Tim McCurdy, Parliament of Victoria
Tim McCurdy, Wikipedia
